主要内容: On June 3, 2019, Cypress Semiconductor Corporation and Infineon Technologies AG announced a merger agreement, under which Infineon would acquire Cypress. The merger would see Cypress continue as a wholly owned subsidiary of Infineon. The deal was structured through a merger of Merger Sub, a subsidiary of Infineon, with Cypress. The transaction was subject to the terms and conditions outlined in the Merger Agreement. This acquisition aimed to strengthen Infineon's position in the semiconductor industry by combining Cypress's expertise in non-volatile memory and programmable system-on-chip solutions with Infineon's existing capabilities. The merger was expected to enhance Infineon's product portfolio and expand its market reach. The deal was a significant move in the semiconductor sector, reflecting the strategic importance of combining complementary technologies and market positions. Infineon has entered into a merger agreement with Cypress, which outlines the terms of the acquisition. Under the agreement, shareholders of Cypress will receive $23.85 in cash per share. Additionally, outstanding options, restricted stock units (RSUs), and performance-based share units (PSUs) will be converted into cash payments based on the Per Share Merger Consideration. The RSU Consideration will vest and be payable on the applicable vesting date, unless a Qualifying Termination occurs, which would accelerate the payment. This merger is expected to strengthen Infineon's position in the semiconductor industry. Infineon has agreed to acquire Cypress, a semiconductor company, as part of a merger subject to regulatory approvals. The merger is contingent on obtaining clearance from the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS), the European Commission, and the Anti-Monopoly Bureau of the State Administration for Market Regulation in China. Infineon has also agreed to divest certain assets and accept restrictions on Cypress's assets if necessary to secure these approvals. The merger is not subject to a financing condition, but it is subject to customary conditions such as stockholder approval and the absence of any law or order prohibiting the transaction. The merger is also subject to a deadline of December 3, 2019, which may be extended under certain circumstances. The merger agreement outlines the terms and conditions of the transaction, including the rights and obligations of both parties.
